bull_bear.body: Board recommended 150% final dividend (INR1.5/share); net cash position INR231cr; no M&A plans announced, but open to opportunistic inorganic growth at good valuations
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: West Asia conflict driving raw material shortages (aluminum, polymers, sulfuric acid); prolonged inflationary pressure; channel inventory imbalances in non-South; new entrants in Wires and Fans; monsoon variability impacting demand
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident and proactive; emphasized pricing leadership, supply chain resilience, and long-term integration strategy; acknowledged inflation risks but highlighted operational discipline and market share gains; optimistic on FY27 summer demand and margin recovery
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Channel financing covers 35% of business (distributor-level, not category-specific); TPW fan shortages due to plastic resin scarcity, not demand; BLDC in mixer grinders not viable due to low usage hours; Kerala remittances show no material impact yet; solar growth is B2C-focused to preserve pricing power
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- "Net cash as on 30th June 2026 is Rs. 669.58 crore, as against net cash on 30th June 2025 of Rs. 155.32 crore" (Rs 231.16 crore at 31 March 2026) - a near-debt-free balance sheet with Gross Debt of just Rs 7.83 crore against Net Worth of Rs 2,509.90 crore.
- "CFO generation continued to remain strong for Q1 FY27 at Rs. 474.12 crore compared to Rs. 134.45 crore for Q1 FY26."
- "ROE and Core ROCE (excl. cash) at 14.5% and 22.9%, respectively over the last 12 months" (TTM basis); RoCE stated at 17.8% versus 16.1% at 31 March 2026 and 16.7% at 30 June 2025.
- Cash is held substantially in Current Investments of Rs 575.85 crore at 30 June 2026 (Rs 180.70 crore at 31 March 2026; Rs 60.26 crore at 30 June 2025) alongside Cash & Cash Equivalents of Rs 101.56 crore.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Electronics: +22.3% YoY (volume-led, 3% price); Electrical: +15.9% YoY; Consumer Durables: +4.1% YoY (Fans/Air Coolers down, Water Heaters/Kitchen up); Sunflame: +8.6% YoY; South markets: +16.2% YoY; non-South: +11.8% YoY (48% of FY26 revenue); BLDC fans: ~40% of ceiling fan sales
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- "V-Guard Industries Limited (BSE:532953, NSE: VGUARD) is a Kochi based company, founded in 1977 by Kochouseph Chittilappilly to manufacture and market Voltage stabilizers", which "has since then established a strong brand name and aggressively diversified to become a multi-product Company catering to the Light Electricals sector".
- "V-Guard has been a dominant player in the South market, though the last ten years have also seen the Company expanding rapidly in the non-South geographies with their contribution increasing from 5% of total revenues in FY08 to around 48% of total revenues in FY26."
- Distribution reach is presented as a core asset: "The Company today has a strong network of 35 branches which cover ~1,00,000+ channel partners across the country", serving "direct marketing agents, distributors and retailers".
- Stated organised-market shares by category include Stabilizers 40-45% (market Rs 1,600-2,000 Cr), Solar Water Heaters 15-17%, Water Heaters 14-16%, Pumps 9-12%, House Wiring Cables 8-9%, Electric Fans 5-7%, DUPS & Battery 5-7%, Switchgears ~5%; named competitors include Polycab, Finolex, Havells, Crompton, Bajaj, Microtek and Legrand.
- Segment mix in Q1 FY27: Electricals 37.0% of revenue, Electronics 36.4%, Consumer Durables 23.0%, Sunflame 3.6%.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Sunflame acquisition] The deck reports two parallel P&Ls, "including Sunflame" and "excluding Sunflame"; Sunflame contributed Rs 65.69 Cr of Q1 FY27 revenue (3.6% of total, +18.3% YoY) at a 4.0% segment margin, and its integration is described as "largely done and under stabilization".
- [Labour codes] The FY26 columns carry an "Exceptional item*" of Rs 22.11 Cr (including Sunflame) / Rs 21.34 Cr (excluding Sunflame), footnoted "* Impact of New Labour Codes"; no exceptional item is shown in Q1 FY27, Q1 FY26, Q4 FY26 or FY25.
- [Geopolitical risk] The MD cites "challenges posed by the West Asia War" as a live risk to supplies and margins, with the company saying it will "take appropriate actions necessary to protect supplies and margins".
- [Market sizing basis] Product market-size tables are footnoted "*Market estimates of VG active product segments only", so the shares shown are share of the indicative organised market, not of total market.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: Gross margin held at 35.3% despite 8-13% input cost inflation (aluminum, polymers, sulfuric acid); pricing action 75% complete, remaining 25% to flow in May-June; EBITDA margin FY26 at 8.8% (ex-one-off: 9.2%); targeting 10%+ EBITDA in FY27 if demand and cost stability improve
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: revenue growth: 10-12% volume + 1-2% price (targeting ~15% total); margin: targeting 10%+ EBITDA margin if summer demand holds; order inflow: not specified; capex/commissioning: no new capex announced, past INR300-400cr investments fully deployed
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Solar inverters: fast-growing residential segment (not yet INR500cr, but potential to become major category in 3-4 years); Kitchen Appliances: post-integration traction with Sunflame; BLDC adoption expanding to chimneys; Lighting: product launch expected early Q1FY27
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: V-Guard delivered strong Q4 revenue and profit growth driven by volume-led Electronics and Electrical segment expansion, with gross margins held steady despite 8-13% input cost inflation; the company is proactively passing on pricing (75% done) and leveraging integrated manufacturing and GTM synergies to navigate supply shocks and position for double-digit EBITDA in FY27.

risks.note: Copper and aluminium are critical inputs forming an essential part of the cost base for consumer durables manufacturers. Copper prices rose to record levels during the year on AI data-centre and green-technology demand, while aluminium markets faced a structural supply shock; firms across the sector had to implement price increases in response to the escalation in key raw-material costs.

The Middle East war disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and damaged production facilities in a region central to hydrocarbon supply, straining global supply chains, surging energy prices and raising the likelihood of a broader economic slowdown; escalating geopolitical tensions generated macroeconomic headwinds towards the close of the financial year.
risks.risk: Geopolitical conflict and energy-supply / supply-chain shock

risks.note: The US imposed a minimum 10% tariff on many foreign goods with higher rates for India, and India faced an effective 50% export tariff on most merchandise goods to the US from August 6, 2025 before reduction to 10% in February 2026 - a volatile policy backdrop for trade flows and input sourcing.
risks.risk: Trade protectionism and tariff regime uncertainty

risks.note: Identified as a material risk: climate change exposes V-Guard to financial risk from regulations, emission targets, energy-cost volatility and investment in cleaner operations, while physical risks such as heat, water scarcity, floods and supply disruptions may affect operations and supply-chain resilience; decarbonization may cause unplanned cost increases from evolving environmental regulation.
risks.risk: Climate change and decarbonization exposure (BRSR material issue)

risks.note: Inadequate water management and rising water stress can disrupt operations, raise procurement/treatment/compliance costs and reduce efficiency; stricter regulation on water use and discharge creates compliance risk and penalties, while pollution or community impact could damage reputation and stakeholder trust.
risks.risk: Water stress and water-management compliance (BRSR material issue)

risks.note: Seasonal variability shaped short-term sectoral performance dynamics, and demand conditions remained uneven across parts of the consumer durables sector - a structural exposure for a portfolio weighted to weather-linked categories.

The Bureau of Energy Efficiency revised mandatory star labelling for a broad range of appliances effective January 1, 2026, tightening efficiency standards and making high-star-rated products more expensive; GST 2.0 effective September 22, 2025 reset appliance tax rates - both reshape product cost, pricing and portfolio economics.
risks.risk: Regulatory change in energy-efficiency and tax norms

risks.note: Pursuant to the new Labour Codes notified in November 2025, an incremental charge towards gratuity and leave encashment provisions was recognised as an exceptional item, and management attributed the year's decline in Return on Net Worth largely to it - a recurring cost-base risk from labour regulation.
risks.risk: New Labour Codes raising employee-benefit obligations
